title: QUIZ_SCHEMA expresses 'exactly 4 options' as prose, not as a constraint
detail: options is an unbounded STRING array whose only statement of intent is description: 'Array of 4 possible answers.' Gemini's schema dialect supports minItems/maxItems and neither is used, so zero options is a schema-valid response. This is the root cause of S106 — a card with no options permanently deadlocks the review queue — and it is fixable at the declaration rather than defended against at every consumer.

title: correctAnswerIndex is an unbounded NUMBER where it should be a bounded INTEGER
detail: The description says 'Index (0-3)' but the declared type is Type.NUMBER with no minimum or maximum, so -1, 99 and 3.7 all satisfy the schema. Type.INTEGER exists in the SDK and is not used. options[3.7] is undefined, which is exactly how a user answers correctly and still scores zero (S062).

title: The schema marks nine fields required while the TypeScript type marks all nine optional
detail: GENERIC_BOOK_SCHEMA.required lists every field; RawBookResponse declares every field optional, with a comment conceding 'a model can always omit one, schema or not'. Both cannot be the contract. The comment is right and the optional type is the safer choice — but that makes `required` decorative, and nothing anywhere reconciles the two or fails loudly when the model does omit one.

title: rating and readingTimeMinutes are unbounded numbers described in prose as bounded
detail: rating says 'from 1 to 5' and readingTimeMinutes implies a positive duration; neither declares minimum or maximum. A rating of 40 is persisted and rendered as stars, and a negative reading time flows straight into the Total Learning figure on the stats page.

title: A second confirm() before the first settles strands the first promise forever
detail: resolverRef.current is overwritten without settling the previous resolver, so the earlier `await confirm(...)` never resolves and its calling function never continues — no error, no timeout, just a dead async call. Double-clicking a delete control, or any two code paths racing to confirm, reproduces it.

title: The focus trap traps Tab but leaves the background readable to screen readers
detail: Nothing sets inert or aria-hidden on the content behind the panel. Keyboard Tab cycling is handled correctly, but a screen-reader user in browse mode walks straight out of the dialog into the library underneath it, which is the failure mode aria-modal alone does not prevent in practice.

title: Focus restoration silently drops to body when the trigger is gone
detail: restoreTo?.focus() assumes the opening element still exists. Deleting a book from its detail page unmounts the trigger, so focus lands on <body> and a keyboard user restarts from the top of the document with no announcement.

title: Backdrop click discards a half-filled form with no warning
detail: Every Dialog closes on any backdrop click. AddBookModal can hold a title, author, rating and a selected PDF; one stray click outside the panel throws all of it away with no confirmation and no restore.

title: crypto.randomUUID() again — the third module that breaks outside a secure context
detail: repo.ts, srs.ts and toastStore.ts all call it directly. On a plain-HTTP deploy the failure is not confined to storage: raising any toast, including the one reporting the original error, throws its own TypeError.

title: The toast queue is unbounded
detail: Module-level array with no cap. A retry loop or a burst of failures stacks toasts indefinitely with nothing evicting the oldest.
